key_insight: A five-agent “Trust but Verify” loop significantly reduced medical hallucinations by catching banned-drug recommendations after the LLM generated them.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLM-based clinical tools can be made safer by adding post-hoc regulatory checks before outputs reach users.
method: Built a five-agent auditing system around a single LLM backbone
Created 103 adversarial clinical MCQs featuring historically correct but now banned substances
Compared vanilla vs agentic performance across GPT-OSS, Llama-3, and Falcon-3
evidence_signal: Across open-access models, the agentic setup reduced Hallucination Error Rate by about 53% and moved pointwise scores from -0.25 toward 0.0.
watch_item: The approach depends on up-to-date regulatory data and careful integration, and it may still miss errors if the audit layer is outdated or incomplete.
paper_title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
